note: Triage of every advisory at or above the fail threshold on master at the commit above. One entry per (advisory, package) — a GHSA id can appear under more than one package, and GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9 does so here (vitest and @vitest/mocker). Entries are suppressions WITH AN EXPIRY: past reviewBy, the scheduled lane fails while the advisory is still live. Advisories below the fail threshold are reported, not baselined, so one escalating into moderate arrives as a new finding. See runbooks/dependency-audit.md.

entries.title: Node.js Adapter for Hono: Path traversal in `serve-static` on Windows via encoded backslash (`%5C`)
entries.introducedVia: every MCP server package via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.1 > @hono/node-server@1.19.13
entries.reason: Two advisories with different floors. GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9 is fixed within 1.x (>=1.19.15) and is a Windows-only serve-static path traversal; GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f needs >=2.1.3, a major bump of a package @modelcontextprotocol/sdk pins as a peer of hono, so it cannot be floored independently of the SDK. entries.title: Vitest: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via @vitest/mocker Redirect Mock
entries.reason: Not in any shipped path: `server/package.json` declares vitest only in devDependencies, and the ONLY edge that puts it in `pnpm audit --prod` scope is better-auth@1.7.14 declaring `vitest` a peerDependency with peerDependenciesMeta.vitest.optional = true. With autoInstallPeers: true, pnpm records the dev-installed vitest in better-auth's peer-resolution key and --prod walks that edge. This is a scoping artefact of optional peers, not a claim the advisory is wrong. It flips the moment vitest becomes a real runtime dependency of anything, which is what the review-by date is for.
